Technical & price structure: In plain terms: Ma'aden trades well above our weighted central fair value — richly valued on every fundamental lens, and priced less as a miner than as the Kingdom's sovereign-backed minerals champion. It runs a world-class, gas-advantaged phosphate business (a ~47% EBITDA margin), a full aluminium chain, and a ramping gold and base-metals unit, with a large new-minerals and exploration pipeline behind it. But at ~15.6× EV/EBITDA and ~31× earnings it is priced at roughly double the multiple of global mining peers — the premium is the Vision-2030 growth story, not today's cash flows. The bull case (~SAR 57) is a strong commodity deck plus full credit for the Phosphate 3 and gold-doubling pipeline; the cautious case (~SAR 27) is a fade in commodity prices and a peer-multiple re-rating. What moves it is the commodity deck — DAP, aluminium, gold — and whether the multi-year growth capex earns its cost of capital.

How is the Ma'aden valuation calculated? — The study triangulates four lenses — a sum-of-the-parts by commodity segment (the primary lens); an explicit five-year discounted cash flow; a relative-multiples cross-check; and a through-cycle mid-cycle-earnings view — then expresses the result as a 50,000-path Monte Carlo probability distribution. Over 57 resolved three-month forecasts, the price finished inside the 90% band 88% of the time, against the 90% that band aims at. The band is 1.03 times the width of a simple no-forecast rule’s — the price of covering this name honestly. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.
